content.text: {"answer":"Cross trades are permitted only when: (1) the portfolio manager determines the transaction is in the best interest of both accounts and consistent with each account's guidelines; (2) the Chief Compliance Officer or Deputy Chief Compliance Officer approves it in advance; and (3) it is executed at the current evaluated price from the Firm's independent primary pricing service. No commission, markup or other compensation is received by the Firm or any affiliate, and cross trades are not effected for any account whose IMA or governing law prohibits them. The Firm does not engage in principal transactions and does not effect agency cross transactions, because it has no affiliated broker-dealer.","source_document":"01_brochure.md","section":"Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.3 Cross Trades; and 11.4 Principal Transactions","quote":"The Firm may effect a cross trade between two client accounts, in which one account sells a security to another, only when the portfolio manager has determined that the transaction is in the best interest of both accounts and consistent with each account's guidelines; the Chief Compliance Officer or the Deputy Chief Compliance Officer has approved the transaction in advance; and the transaction is executed at the current evaluated price supplied by the Firm's independent primary pricing service. Neither the Firm nor any affiliate receives a commission, markup or other compensation in connection with a cross trade. Cross trades are not effected for any account whose IMA or governing law prohibits them. ... The Firm does not engage in principal transactions, in which the Firm or an affiliate buys a security from or sells a security to a client for its own account, and it does not effect agency cross transactions, because it has no affiliated broker-dealer."}
